LESSON: READING 14.4.1 FEATURES OF STYLE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Features of style

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 14.4.1 Features of style. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: where dialogues, similes, and metaphors can be used. Why do we use stylistic devices in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text
2. use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text
   In simple words: practise until you can identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context
   In simple words: practise until you can use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 14.4.1 Features of style using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 14.4.1 Features of style in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 14.4.1 Features of style to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 14.4.1 Features of style.
4. Show that you can: identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 14.4.1 Features of style using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 14.4.1 Features of style important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read the class reader and identify with illustrations, instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text, and display their work on the class notice boards,
2. Role-play selected dialogues from the class reader and record themselves for video sharing and review,
3. Make sentences using the similes and metaphors identified from the text,
4. Self-efficacy: It is developed as the learner holds a discussion on instances in real life where dialogues, similes, and metaphors can be used, thereby enhancing their literary skills.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text
2. use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
